summary: The article provides a largely accurate overview of the Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme (SCSS) rules, interest rates, and common mistakes, with most factual claims verified against authoritative sources.

claims.claim: The Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme (SCSS) currently offers an attractive interest rate of 8.2% for the October-December 2026 quarter.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm the SCSS interest rate of 8.2% for the October-December 2026 quarter.

claims.claim: Retirees can now invest a maximum of ₹30 lakh in SCSS, providing a stable income stream.
claims.note: The maximum investment limit for SCSS was increased to ₹30 lakh per individual.

claims.claim: If your total interest income from all SCSS accounts (and other sources like bank FDs) exceeds a certain threshold in a financial year, the bank or post office will deduct Tax Deducted at Source (TDS). For senior citizens (aged 60 and above), the TDS threshold for interest income is ₹1,00,000 per financial year, effective from FY 2025-26. For non-senior citizens (e.g., those investing under VRS between 55-60 years), the TDS threshold is ₹50,000 per financial year, effective from FY 2025-26.
claims.note: The TDS threshold for senior citizens was raised to ₹1,00,000 from FY 2025-26. For non-senior citizens, the threshold is ₹50,000. This is consistent across multiple sources.

claims.claim: If your total income is below the taxable limit, you can submit Form 15H (for senior citizens) or Form 15G (for others) to the bank or post office to avoid TDS deduction. Remember to submit this form at the beginning of each financial year.
claims.note: From April 2026, Form 15H has been replaced by Form 121 for senior citizens to avoid TDS. Form 15G is still applicable for non-senior citizens.

claims.claim: Withdrawal within 1 year: No interest is paid, and the entire deposit is refunded.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm that no interest is paid if withdrawn within 1 year, and any interest already paid is recovered from the principal.

claims.claim: Withdrawal after 1 year but before 2 years: 1.5% of the deposit amount is deducted as penalty.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm a 1.5% penalty for withdrawals after 1 year but before 2 years.

claims.claim: Withdrawal after 2 years but before 5 years: 1% of the deposit amount is deducted as penalty.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm a 1% penalty for withdrawals after 2 years but before 5 years.

claims.claim: After the initial 5-year tenure, you have the option to extend your SCSS account for another 3 years. This extension must be applied for within one year of the account maturity. The interest rate applicable for the extended period will be the rate prevailing on the date of extension.
claims.note: SCSS accounts can be extended for 3-year blocks, and the application must be made within one year of maturity. The interest rate for the extended period is the rate prevailing on the date of extension. It's also worth noting that multiple extensions are now allowed, which the article implies but doesn't explicitly state in this claim. However, the core of the claim is correct.

article_title: SCSS Investment Rules: Avoid These 5 Mistakes Before Investing ₹30 Lakh
